visible_constraints: Refund can be requested only while order has no other active request
Complete refund available only while refund pending; terminal, one-time completion
Cancel order locks all further order actions
Price adjustment can only be requested once
observed_changes: "Request refund" button REMAINED VISIBLE and availableActions.requestRefund REMAINED true

roles.name: customer
roles.note: No login/authentication endpoint was recorded in any source run; the app appears to serve a single anonymous order view (order #1042) with no session cookies or bearer tokens observed. Not reported as a missing-auth vulnerability per scope: authentication_required is not set in scope.json.

conflicting_action_pairs.state: order delivered, no request active (fresh order, each observed independently across three source runs)
conflicting_action_pairs.rule: At most one order-value-returning action (price adjustment, refund, cancellation) should ever be permitted per order; the UI presents them as mutually exclusive ("another order request is active") and cancel/refund correctly disable each other and price adjustment. However, price-adjustment does NOT disable requestRefund server-side or client-side.
Cancellation and refund completion must not both reimburse the same order

critical_endpoints.why: Issues a $30 payout and is the ONLY one of the three order-value-returning actions whose response does not set availableActions.requestRefund to false, unlike refund/request and cancel which both correctly lock out the other two actions. Agent inference (unverified): this asymmetry may allow a customer to collect a price adjustment ($30) AND a full refund ($100) on the same $100 order (totalReturned=130 > originalAmount=100), a direct financial-loss / double-dip vulnerability.
Creates a $100 refund request; correctly disables cancelOrder, requestPriceAdjustment and itself, but was never observed being called AFTER a price adjustment already completed on the same order.
Completes the payout for a pending refund; terminal one-time action per UIR-002 (refund-rerun). Never tested for replay after completion or after order was independently canceled/adjusted.
Issues a $100 reimbursement and correctly disables all other actions (cleanest lock observed across the three flows).
